propositions: VOTER_ERROR markers are emitted twice per incident (once to logger, once to stderr print) when logging is configured, causing the observability probe's anchored journald grep to count each error twice and double the voter_errors metric

The root cause is that configure_logging() attaches a StreamHandler(sys.stdout) that captures logger.error(line) calls containing the line-start marker token, while the same line is also unconditionally printed to stderr, resulting in two identically-timestamped journald records per real error
Sibling markers MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, RECONCILE_DEGRADED, ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR, and LLM_TOKEN_USAGE exhibit the same dual-emission construct and suffer the same doubling problem

The fix removes the token-prefixed marker string from all logger calls, logging only the structured record body instead, while preserving the unconditional stderr print as the single canonical line-start emission that journald can count
A structural class-guard test prevents future markers from reintroducing the dual line-start emission construct
